implies that the simple root directions of
$T\subset B\subset G$ are the simple coroot directions of
$T^{\vee}_{\mathbf{k}}\subset\widetilde{B}\subset\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}}$ :

$\bigl\{\mathbf{Q}_{+}\cdot\alpha:\alpha\in\Delta^{\vee}_{\mathrm{s}}(\widetilde{G}_{\mathbf{k}},\widetilde{B},T^{\vee}_{\mathbf{k}})\bigr\}=\bigl\{\mathbf{Q}_{+}\cdot\beta:\beta\in\Delta_{\mathrm{s}}(G,B,T)\bigr\}.$

(9.2)

(In fact, these sets are the extreme rays of the rational convex polyhedral cone determined by $\{\lambda\in\mathbf{Q}\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}X^{*}(T)\mid\forall\mu\in X_{*}(T)^{+},\ \langle\lambda,\mu\rangle\geq 0\}$ .)
card.label: Lemma 9.5

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
